summary: Saroja Bhate is an Indologist and linguist who served as Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1978–2002) and Honorary Secretary at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~2002–2007).

Sarva Daman Singh worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. His career included holding a post at the University of Queensland, where he was attested as Professor of History in 1958 and attested again in 1987.

Sarvepalli Gopal (1923–2002) was a historian who studied at Mill Hill School, Madras Christian College, Presidency College, Chennai, the University of Madras, and Balliol College, Oxford. He held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University from ~1971 to 1983.

Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1888–1975) worked in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies, studying at Madras Christian College under Alfred George Hogg and William Meston. He held professorships at Mysore, Calcutta, and Oxford, and served as Vice-Chancellor of Andhra and Banaras Hindu universities.

Saswati Mutsuddy is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Dipak Kumar Barua. She served on the teaching staff of the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011).
Satiranjan Sen worked in Sinology and Indology, studying at Peking University. He was a Research Scholar and Junior Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati University and founded Cheen Bharat Sanskriti.

Satish Chandra Vidyabhusan (1870–1920) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, studying under Sarat Chandra Das and earning a PhD from the University of Calcutta. He was Principal of Sanskrit College and held posts at the Asiatic Society.

Satkari Mookerjee (1896–1968) was an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (~1948–1955) and became the second director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1955.
Satkari Mukhopadhyaya is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who served as Coordinator of the Kala Kosa Division at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (attested 1999, 2026).
Satoru Fujiwara is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a researcher at the Shinran Buddhist Center (attested 2015) and as a lecturer at Otani University (attested 2026).

Satoru Harada (born 1947) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo (~1970–1973). He held posts at Toyo Bunko, Toho Gakuin, and as professor at Kokushikan University (attested 2010–2015).
Satoru Noriyama works in Buddhist studies and studied under Esho Mikogami. He held teaching posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1995) and Ryukoku University (attested 2003, 2013).
Satoshi Hayashima works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied as a research student at Ryukoku University (attested 2013–2014) and later served there as a lecturer (attested 2015–2017).

Satoshi Hiraoka (born 1960) works in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying under Shozen Kumoi, Takao Kagawa, Luis O. Gómez, and Gregory Schopen. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Michigan, later becoming Professor and President of Kyoto Bunkyo University.
Satoshi Ito (born 1961) works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University and served as a professor at Ibaraki University (~2005).
Satoshi Kono (born 1954) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a doctorate in literature from the University of Tokyo. He became a professor at Kogakkan University in 2000.

Satoshi Naiki works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Kyoto University, where he also served as Assistant Professor at the Center for Cultural Heritage Studies (attested 2016–2020).
Satya Narayan Goenka (1924–2013) was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Sayagyi U Ba Khin (~1955–1969). He founded the Vipassana Research Institute in 1985.

Satya Vrat Shastri (1930–2021) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Charu Deva Shastri, Shukdev Jha, and Siddheshwar Varma at Punjab, Banaras Hindu, and Punjabi universities. He held professorships at Delhi and served as Vice-Chancellor of Shri Jagannath Sanskrit Vishvavidyalaya.

Satyendra Nath Bose (1894–1974) studied at Presidency College, Kolkata, and the University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture. He taught at Dhaka University (1921–1945), Calcutta University (1945–1956), and served as Vice-Chancellor of Visva-Bharati University (~1956–1958).
